title: Examining the Impact of Crowding Perception on the Generation of Negative Emotions among Users of Small Urban Micro Public Spaces
research_question: This study aims to test the hypothesis that crowding in urban micro public spaces (UMPSs) affects emotions, and to explore whether user-perceived crowding promotes negative emotions, influences environmental attractiveness and revisit intentions, and if environmental attractiveness moderates the effect of perceived crowding on revisiting intentions.

participants.description: Questionnaire: 567 valid responses. EEG: 18 participants (9 males, 11 females initially, 18 final dataset). Participants were from Shenyang, China, with a focus on middle-aged and elderly individuals (43.21% aged 18-45, 55.56% aged 46-65).
participants.recruitment: Questionnaire: random sampling method online. EEG: 18 participants selected from different age groups based on questionnaire responses.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: Separate pictures representing two categories of small urban micro public spaces: crowded and uncrowded conditions.

measures.instrument: Emotional Experience Scale / Mood Experience Scale (5 items, Likert-type)
Emotional Experience Scale / Mood Experience Scale (5 items, Likert-type)
7 items from Hu and Ritchie [54] and Li et al. [37] (Likert-type)

findings.quote: The coefficient of crowding on positive emotions was –0.212 and statistically significant (p < 0.05)

findings.mechanism: Crowding induces stress and elicits negative emotions.
findings.quote: the coefficient of crowding perception on negative emotions was 0.221 and significant (p < 0.05)

findings.mechanism: Negative emotional experiences due to crowding lead to a disliking for revisiting such environments.
findings.quote: the coefficient of crowding perception on revisit intention was -0.218 and significant (p < 0.05)

findings.mechanism: Positive emotions enhance well-being and amplify health benefits, leading to higher revisit intentions.
findings.quote: the coefficient of positive emotions on revisit intention was 0.392 and significant (p < 0.05)

findings.mechanism: Negative emotional states compromise cognitive abilities and decrease likelihood of revisiting.
findings.quote: the coefficient of negative emotions on revisit intention was −0.443 and significant (p < 0.05)

findings.quote: mediation effect of -0.083 from crowding perception to positive emotion to revisit intention.

findings.mechanism: Negative emotions mediate the relationship between crowding perception and revisit intention.
findings.quote: mediation effect of -0.098 from crowding perception to negative emotion to revisit intention

findings.mechanism: When environmental attractiveness was high, the positive impact of positive emotion on revisit intention became more pronounced and influential.

findings.mechanism: When environmental attractiveness was low, the detrimental impact of negative emotion on revisit intention was more pronounced.
findings.quote: Negative emotions * Environmental appeal β: 0.406 ... p-Value: 0.000

findings.quote: the analysis indicated that the mediating effect was inconsistent at different levels, indicating a moderating mediating effect.

findings.mechanism: At low levels of environmental attractiveness, there was no mediating effect of positive emotions between crowding perception and revisit intention.
findings.quote: at low levels, the boot 95% CI included the number 0 at low levels, which suggested that there was no mediating effect at this level

findings.mechanism: At mean levels of environmental attractiveness, positive emotions mediate the relationship between crowding perception and revisit intention.
findings.quote: at the mean level, the boot 95% CI did not include the number 0, indicating a mediating effect at this level

findings.mechanism: At high levels of environmental attractiveness, positive emotions mediate the relationship between crowding perception and revisit intention.
findings.quote: at high levels, the absence of the number 0 in the boot 95% CI represented a mediating effect at this level

findings.mechanism: The mediating effect of negative emotions between crowding perception and revisit intention is inconsistent across different levels of environmental attractiveness.
findings.quote: the analysis revealed inconsistent mediating effects at different levels, indicating a moderating mediating effect.

findings.mechanism: At low levels of environmental attractiveness, negative emotions mediate the relationship between crowding perception and revisit intention.
findings.quote: At low levels, the bootstrapped 95% CI did not include zero, which indicated a significant mediating effect at this level

findings.mechanism: At mean levels of environmental attractiveness, negative emotions mediate the relationship between crowding perception and revisit intention.
findings.quote: At the mean level, the bootstrapped 95% CI also did not include zero, which can suggest a significant mediating effect

findings.mechanism: At high levels of environmental attractiveness, there was no mediating effect of negative emotions between crowding perception and revisit intention.
findings.quote: at high levels, the bootstrapped 95% CI includes zero, indicating no mediating effect at this level.

findings.mechanism: Decreased activity in the right temporal lobe during crowded conditions triggered negative emotion.
findings.quote: The crowded stimulus exhibited weaker activation in the right temporal lobe compared to the uncrowded condition

findings.mechanism: Decreased activity in the left hemisphere beta band during crowded conditions triggered negative emotion.
findings.quote: in the beta band, the left hemisphere indicated reduced activation compared to the uncrowded condition.

findings.mechanism: Heightened activation in the brain's temporal lobe elicits positive emotional responses.
findings.quote: the uncrowded environment of a small urban micro public space facilitates heightened activation in the brain's temporal lobe

mechanisms: Crowding induces stress and elicits negative emotions, which can compromise cognitive abilities and reduce revisit intentions.
Emotional reactions (positive and negative) mediate the relationship between crowding perception and revisit intentions.
Environmental attractiveness moderates the influence of emotions on revisit intentions, either amplifying positive effects or attenuating negative ones.
Crowding leads to reduced attentional control and higher physiological arousal.
Uncrowded environments facilitate heightened activation in the brain's temporal lobe, eliciting positive emotional responses.
implementation_implications: Optimize the design of urban micro and small public spaces (UMPSs) to foster positive urban emotions.
Enhance the equitable availability, accessibility, and attractiveness of UMPSs.
Provide comfortable, relaxed, and safe environments in UMPSs to mitigate negative emotions from crowding.
Improve environmental management, optimize public infrastructure layout, and increase the number of UMPSs in crowded areas to disperse people flow.
Building UMPSs can promote people's health and contribute to sustainable urban development.

tables.description: Classification of small and micro public spaces in urban areas.
Situation of small urban micro public space near residential areas.
Standardized parameter estimates for the structural model and hypothesis testing.

limitations: Generalization of findings should be cautious due to potential variations in crowding perceptions across different seasons and environmental factors.
Specialized EEG equipment is needed for capturing data in diverse environmental contexts.
The EEG equipment was primarily suited for controlled indoor environments, limiting the presented environment and the number of stimuli.
The experimental design only allowed for between-subjects analysis of subjective experience and environmental evaluations.
Future work should investigate how other types of urban environments and multiple levels of social density interact with attention, cognition, and subjective experience.
Future studies should enhance EEG equipment for on-site data collection in UMPSs to capture nuanced emotional dynamics.
The sample size of psychometric measurements was significant but could not be matched by the EEG measurements, making psychometric results primary and physiological indices secondary.

paper_metadata.title: Examining the Impact of Crowding Perception on the Generation of Negative Emotions among Users of Small Urban Micro Public Spaces
paper_metadata.crossref_title: Examining the Impact of Crowding Perception on the Generation of Negative Emotions among Users of Small Urban Micro Public Spaces
paper_metadata.crossref_abstract: The improvement of urban congestion and the mood of the populace is vital for achieving the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. This paper aims to test the hypothesis that crowding in urban micro public spaces (UMPSs) affects emotions, and two different methods were used: a psychological questionnaire to measure whether crowding in such spaces elicits negative emotional responses from users and a portable electroencephalography (EEG) device to explore emotional responses. This study was conducted in Shenyang, China, based on the city’s relevant policies and the type and number of micro spaces and micro public spaces, proving that Shenyang City has paid more attention to planning micro spaces and micro public spaces in its urban development. The results show that 1. UMPS crowding awakens negative emotions in users, which affects their intention to revisit the UMPS, and 2. If the UMPS is more attractive to users, it also improves the negative emotions due to crowding, which implies that the attractiveness of the environment does play an important moderating role. This study may inspire the construction concept of UMPSs in different countries and cities, complementing the planning of urban public spaces to provide more social equity. The creation of UMPS has a positive effect on neighborhood interactions, community network construction, and the reproduction of social capital, which can contribute to the sustainable development of cities.
